paragraphs.text: Wszolek et al. (1995) described a large family (family D) from western Nebraska whose ancestors had probably immigrated to the United States from England. The family included 188 individuals spanning 6 generations, 18 of whom were affected. Affected members had typical levodopa-responsive Parkinson disease with bradykinesia, rigidity, resting tremor, and impaired postural reflexes. Eye movement abnormalities, pyramidal and cerebellar signs, sensory disturbances, and orthostatic blood pressure changes did not occur. The disease progressed slowly. In one affected member, PET with [18F]-6-fluoro-L-dopa showed decreased fluorodopa uptake in a pattern consistent with PD. Autopsy of another affected member showed neuronal and pigmentary loss, gliosis, and Lewy bodies in the substantia nigra pars compacta. The authors concluded that the disorder closely resembled, if it was not identical to, idiopathic PD.

paragraphs.text: Hasegawa and Kowa (1997) reported a family from Sagamihara City, Japan, with Parkinson disease in 5 generations. Clinically, the disease did not differ from common PD. Onset was at an older age, and the response to levodopa therapy was good. The neuropathology in autopsied family members differed from that of typical PD. Loss of melanin-containing cells was mild to moderate, and the number of locus ceruleus neurons was maintained. No Lewy bodies were found in any of the regions where Lewy bodies are often seen in PD.

(2011) gave the UPSIT to 31 patients with Parkinson disease associated with LRRK2 G2019S (manifesting carriers), 30 patients with PD who did not carry the mutation, 28 carrier relatives without PD (nonmanifesting carriers), and 46 controls. Compared with controls, mean scores were lower in nonmanifesting carriers (difference = -3.518, p = 0.006), manifesting carriers (difference = -7.677), and noncarrier PD patients (difference = -13.810). The authors concluded that olfaction is impaired in G2019S-related PD, but less overall than in other PD. Olfaction was also impaired in a subset of the nonmanifesting carriers. They compared these levels with PET measures of striatal dopaminergic function using 18F-6-fluoro-L-dopa (FD), 11C-dihydrotetrabenazine, and 11C-d-threo-methylphenidate. Lower CSF Abeta42 and tau levels correlated with lower striatal dopaminergic function on all 3 tracers, and the association between Abeta42 and FD uptake was significant. When the analysis was limited to carriers of G2019S, the most common LRRK2 variant in the cohort, the correlations with tau were also significant. The authors concluded that how amyloid beta and tau are handled is likely important in both LRRK2-related and sporadic PD, even early in the disease. They suggested that these CSF proteins might serve as biomarkers of early or presymptomatic disease.

paragraphs.text: Gehrke et al. (2010) proposed that pathogenic LRRK2 impairs microRNA (miRNA)-mediated translational repression. In flies, ubiquitous or dopaminergic neuron-specific expression of pathogenic Drosophila dLRRK I1915T or human LRRK2 G2019S stimulated expression of an in vivo reporter carrying let-7-binding sites more than the wildtype proteins did. dLRRK RNAi decreased reporter expression, and kinase-dead dLRRK had no effect. Reporter mRNA levels were unchanged. In HEK293T cells, LRRK2 I2020T or G2019S efficiently suppressed let-7 inhibition of a luciferase reporter, and adding kinase-inactivating mutations abolished this effect. By coimmunoprecipitation, LRRK2 associated with Argonaute proteins of the RNA-induced silencing complex (human Ago2 and Drosophila Ago1), apparently directly rather than through RNA. Pathogenic LRRK2 did not change let-7 levels. The authors concluded that LRRK2 antagonizes let-7 function at the translational level in a kinase-dependent manner.

paragraphs.text: Gehrke et al. (2010) found that 4E-BP1 associated with human Ago2, and that dLRRK I1915T and LRRK2 G2019S promoted this association more effectively than the wildtype proteins, presumably through increased phosphorylation of 4E-BP1. Phosphomimetic 4E-BP attenuated let-7 effects and was toxic to dopaminergic neurons. Nonphosphorylatable 4E-BP blocked the ability of LRRK2 G2019S to antagonize let-7. Translational profiling of fly heads identified e2f1 and dp as targets whose translation is upregulated by pathogenic LRRK2, through a miR-184*-binding site in the e2f1 3-prime UTR and a let-7-binding site in the dp 3-prime UTR. E2F1 and DP protein levels were increased by pathogenic dLRRK or LRRK2 and decreased in dLRRK-null mutants, without changes in mRNA level. Removing 1 copy of e2f1 or dp, or overexpressing the negative regulator RBF, suppressed the dopaminergic neuron phenotypes and oxidative stress sensitivity of dLRRK I1915T animals. Pathogenic dLRRK did not affect the activities of the bantam and miR-14 miRNAs in the eye, suggesting miRNA- or tissue-specific regulation. The authors concluded that pathogenic LRRK2 antagonizes let-7 and miR-184*, causing overproduction of E2F1/DP, which in postmitotic neurons may lead to abortive cell division and cell death. Because LRRK2 effects appeared only in aged animals, they suggested that LRRK2 is particularly important for miRNA regulation under stress.

(2010) screened 953 patients with early-onset Parkinson disease (onset at 50 years or younger) from 13 movement disorders centers, recruited without regard to family history. Grandparents' country of origin was known for 11 of the 15 non-Jewish carriers. Four reported Southern European descent (Italy or Portugal), 4 mixed European descent, 1 Eastern European ancestry, and 2 Puerto Rican ancestry.

paragraphs.text: Liu et al. (2008) used the GAL4/UAS system to generate transgenic Drosophila expressing wildtype human LRRK2 or LRRK2 G2019S. Expression of either form in photoreceptor cells caused retinal degeneration. Neuronal expression of either form caused adult-onset selective loss of dopaminergic neurons, locomotor dysfunction, and early death. At equivalent expression levels, G2019S caused a more severe parkinsonism-like phenotype than wildtype LRRK2. L-DOPA treatment improved the locomotor impairment but did not prevent loss of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive neurons. The authors considered this, to their knowledge, the first in vivo gain-of-function model to recapitulate several key features of LRRK2-linked human parkinsonism.

paragraphs.text: In Drosophila, Gehrke et al. (2010) found that pathogenic human LRRK2 significantly reduced dAgo1 protein in aged but not young flies, and that dAgo1 was increased in dLRRK mutants. Ago1 heterozygosity worsened the climbing defect and dopaminergic neuron loss in pathogenic dLRRK or LRRK2 transgenics. Dicer1 overexpression suppressed dLRRK I1915T toxicity, and Dicer1 RNAi worsened it. Overexpression or injection of let-7 or miR-184* lowered DP or E2F1 levels, respectively, and partially rescued dLRRK I1915T phenotypes. Loss of miRNA function phenocopied pathogenic LRRK2. Let-7 mutants had reduced locomotor activity and a specific reduction in dopaminergic neurons. Antagomirs against let-7 or miR-184* raised DP or E2F1 levels and caused dopaminergic neuron loss and reduced climbing, effects attenuated by e2f1 or dp heterozygosity. E2F1 overexpression alone was enough to cause dopaminergic neuron degeneration. Disrupting the let-7/dp interaction, either with a dp target protector or with genomic dp transgenes lacking functional let-7-binding sites, caused DP accumulation, dopaminergic neuron loss, and locomotor defects.

paragraphs.text: Lee et al. (2010) developed a mouse model of LRRK2 dopaminergic neurotoxicity based on herpes simplex virus (HSV) amplicons. Three weeks after stereotaxic injection into the striatum, HSV-delivered LRRK2 G2019S caused significant loss of ipsilateral tyrosine hydroxylase-positive substantia nigra neurons compared with wildtype LRRK2 and eGFP control viruses. Kinase-dead LRRK2 G2019S/D1994A caused no neuronal loss, despite equivalent overexpression. Twice-daily intraperitoneal injections of the LRRK2 kinase inhibitors GW5074 or indirubin-3-prime-monooxime (2.5 mg/kg) attenuated the neuronal loss compared with controls. GW5074 also rescued the reduced density of TH-positive fibers and prevented the increase in isolectin B4-positive inflammatory cells in the striatum and substantia nigra compacta.
